result.dissent:
The strongest case against ADOPT-WITH-ASKS, steelmanned, and I do not think it is weak:

The honest rule for extraction is three consumers before you generalize. glass-ui extracted at N=1 (speedtest), and the result was objectively overfit garbage — `ping|download|upload|jitter` in a design-system type union, three forked surface recipes, one invented for a single atlas view. Then it rewrote the contract WHOLESALE at 7.0.0 — zero prop overlap, zero slot overlap — again at N=1, with only its own demo story as witness. value.js is now being asked to be the validating second consumer for an abstraction that has already been wrong once at exactly this sample size, and the very first thing value's serious analysis produced was five functional asks on an axis the primitive never considered. That is the same signal that preceded the 4.0.1->7.0.0 rewrite: a real consumer arrives, the primitive does not reach, the contract moves. Binding 15 of 18 routes to that producer, in a repository whose measured delivery rate is 38%, is a schedule-coupling bet on a contract that has demonstrated it will break. And the one thing the chassis genuinely cannot express — Browse/Library's 64–66.7/33.3–36 range — I resolved by editing canon to fit the mechanism, which is precisely the move you make when the tool is driving the design rather than serving it. A skeptic is entitled to say I proved the bespoke is a clone only because I wrote the bespoke to the chassis's own decomposition; a genuinely independent value-native mechanism might not decompose into stage/inspector/action at all, given that not one of value's five configurator panes is shaped that way today — they are single-column self-scrolling Cards, and the chassis is prescribing a shape value has never shipped.

Why I still rule ADOPT-WITH-ASKS despite all of that: the bespoke-delta is arithmetic, not rhetoric. Even granting the skeptic's framing, when I sat down to write value's own mechanism against value's own binding route table, 43 of 64 declarations came out byte-identical — including constants I had to copy out of dist to seven decimals. I could not make it come out otherwise without inventing regions value's routes do not have. And the knob test is the decisive discriminator the count-based argument misses: an overfit abstraction shows up as dead knobs in the second consumer, and value has none — `tone` in particular is a knob value is the ideal consumer of and which was demonstrably not built for it. That is what a genuine minimal contract looks like from the outside. The five asks are additive block-axis arms that leave the center untouched; if they had been "different ratios, a fourth region, different slots," I would have ruled BESPOKE without hesitation.
